title: EFC Background No-Go Theorem: Why Background-Level Modification Cannot Suppress Structure Growth
description: Shows, via three independent parametrisations and a BAO–CMB joint analysis, that any EFC background H(z) modification large enough to improve BAO is decisively ruled out by CMB distance priors. The result is structural (due to DA(z*) integrating through z < 2) and closes Level 3: the EFC background is effectively ΛCDM at current precision, redirecting viable EFC dynamics to the perturbation sector.

background_distance_integrals.description: Key background observables (transverse comoving, radial, and angular diameter distances) as functionals of H(z).

modified_friedmann_linear.description: Linear EFC background coupling tested against BAO and CMB distance priors.

exponential_geff.description: Exponential coupling of the effective gravitational strength to the entropy sigmoid S(a), localising modifications to z \lesssim 1.

piecewise_regime_model.latex: H(z) = \begin{cases} H_{\Lambda\mathrm{CDM}}(z), & z \ge z_{\mathrm{switch}} \\ H_{\mathrm{EFC}}(z), & z < z_{\mathrm{switch}} \end{cases}
piecewise_regime_model.description: Regime-aware, piecewise H(z) meant to confine modifications to low z; empirically equivalent to the global sigmoid model for z_{\mathrm{switch}} \gtrsim 1.5.

da_integral_split.description: Even when high-z physics is standard, DA(z_*) integrates through the low-z modified regime, enforcing a structural BAO–CMB tradeoff.

key_results.main_finding: Any low-z EFC background H(z) modification large enough to improve BAO (Δχ2_BAO ≈ −14.6) is decisively penalized by CMB distance priors (Δχ2_CMB > +100), yielding Δχ2_total ≈ +98 and closing Level 3 as observationally empty at current precision.

sealed_predictions.statement: With current precision, any background-only EFC modification localized at z < 1 that yields Δχ2_BAO ≤ −5 will necessarily incur Δχ2_CMB ≥ +5, so the joint Δχ2_total remains ≥ 0; tightening BAO/CMB errors (e.g., DESI DR3, Euclid) will strengthen this constraint unless perturbation modeling is altered.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: A joint BAO + CMB distance-prior fit in which a background-only f(S) modification achieves Δχ2_total ≤ −5 without invoking perturbation-sector changes (μ, Σ).

kill_criteria: KC1: A robust joint BAO + CMB distance-prior analysis demonstrating a background-only H(z) deviation at z < 1 that improves BAO (Δχ2_BAO ≤ −5) while keeping Δχ2_CMB ≤ +5 (i.e., Δχ2_total ≤ −5).

KC2: Independent low-z distance measurements (e.g., time-delay strong-lensing + SNe Ia with calibrated r_d or standard sirens) requiring a ≥2% change in H(z) over 0.3 < z < 1 that remains consistent with CMB-inferred D_A(z_*), contradicting the claimed structural tradeoff.

KC3: Growth and lensing probes (RSD + weak lensing) jointly demanding μ(a,k) ≥ 1 at z < 1 while also preferring suppressed σ8 relative to ΛCDM, contradicting the EFC perturbation-sector suppression pathway (μ < 1).

analytical.name: Sign Lemma
analytical.statement: ΔE²(z) = A·[g(z) − g(0)] ≤ 0 for all z > 0
analytical.proof: Under closure normalisation E(0) = 1, the gate g(z) is monotonically decreasing for z > 0 (activates at late times). Therefore g(z) ≤ g(0) for all z > 0, and with A > 0, ΔE² ≤ 0.
analytical.corollary: H_EFC(z) ≤ H_ΛCDM(z) → reduced Hubble friction → enhanced structure growth
analytical.implication: Background-level EFC structurally excluded for σ₈ suppression

falsification_criteria.implication: Background gate not empty; observational pillar fails

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper establishes a structural no-go theorem proving that any EFC background H(z) modification observable with current data (BAO+CMB) is decisively ruled out, closing Level 3 (background recovery) as observationally empty. The result is parametrisation-independent — three independent approaches all yield the same structural tradeoff (Δχ²_total ≈ +98) — and redirects all viable EFC phenomenology to the perturbation sector (μ, Σ). This is a critical self-imposed constraint that sharpens the EFC prediction landscape: the background IS ΛCDM at current precision, and the theory's observable signatures live exclusively in growth suppression and lensing modifications.
graph_insights: No related papers found in the graph at 1-2 hops, indicating this is a new structural node that should become a hub — it connects background observables (H(z), BAO, CMB distance priors) to the perturbation sector by exclusion, creating a 'funnel' topology in the knowledge graph where all future test paths must route through perturbation-sector nodes.

The concepts 'regime separation' and 'angular diameter distance' appear together for the first time in the graph, establishing a new edge: the regime architecture's sigmoid transition is constrained not just by theoretical consistency but by the geometric structure of DA(z*). This edge should propagate to any future node touching EFC regime boundaries.

The absence of validation tests sharing observables suggests this paper creates a new observable category: 'background exclusion tests' — these are not traditional fits but structural impossibility proofs. The graph should accommodate this as a distinct test type.

tests_added.name: No-Go Test 1: Linear α·T(a) BAO–CMB joint
tests_added.description: Tests whether linear entropic coupling α·T(a) in the Friedmann equation can improve BAO while remaining consistent with CMB distance priors. Result: α = −0.32 ± 0.40, |Δχ²| < 3, background gate empty.
tests_added.data_source: Planck 2018 CMB distance priors + DESI DR1 BAO
tests_added.prediction: EFC predicts no observable background deviation: any improvement in BAO is penalised by CMB, confirming background ≡ ΛCDM at current precision

tests_added.name: No-Go Test 2: Exponential Geff coupling BAO–CMB joint
tests_added.description: Tests Geff(a) = G0·exp(aG·S(a)) with aG=0.094 against joint BAO+CMB. BAO improves by Δχ²_BAO = −14.6 but CMB penalty is Δχ²_CMB > +112, yielding Δχ²_total ≈ +98. Full (aG, at, σ) grid over 1875 points finds no viable combination.
tests_added.data_source: Planck 2018 CMB distance priors + DESI DR1 BAO (14 pts)
tests_added.prediction: EFC predicts the exponential coupling cannot improve joint fit; background modification is excluded at high significance

implicit_consequences: The EFC perturbation sector (μ < 1, Σ modifications) is now the ONLY observationally viable arena — every future EFC test must target growth or lensing, not expansion history. This massively focuses the testing program.

The sealed prediction for fσ8(z=0.7) = 0.430 becomes even more critical: since background is provably ΛCDM, any growth anomaly detected by DESI DR2 RSD cannot be attributed to background mismodelling — it must be perturbation-sector physics, exactly where EFC predicts its signature.

The no-go theorem provides implicit protection against a class of criticisms: EFC cannot be accused of hiding free parameters in the background expansion because the background is provably locked to ΛCDM. This reduces the effective parameter count of the theory.

Sub-percent background modifications below current sensitivity remain logically possible but are explicitly quarantined as untestable with current data — this sets a clear threshold for when Stage-IV surveys (Euclid, DESI DR2 with tighter rd) could reopen Level 3.

KC3 paper-level kill criteria (requiring μ ≥ 1 from growth+lensing) becomes the sharpest external threat: if RSD+WL data demand gravitational enhancement rather than suppression, EFC's perturbation sector is directly falsified with no background escape hatch.
The DA(z*) integral constraint is survey-independent — it applies equally to Euclid, Roman, and any future BAO survey. Level 3 closure is not contingent on DESI specifically.
